warmup.description: Activate deep core and improve spinal mobility before loading.
movements: Standing torso rotations x 10 per side

main_exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise (or Captain’s Chair)
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight; stop 2-3 reps before losing control or swinging
main_exercises.form_cue: Tilt pelvis slightly upward at the top to engage lower abs rather than hip flexors.

main_exercises.name: Cable or Resistance Band Woodchopper
main_exercises.load_guidance: Moderate resistance that challenges rotation but allows smooth control
main_exercises.form_cue: Rotate through the torso, not just arms, and keep hips relatively stable.

main_exercises.name: Dumbbell Suitcase Carry
main_exercises.load_guidance: Choose a weight that challenges your ability to stay upright without leaning
main_exercises.form_cue: Stand tall and resist side bending; imagine balancing a glass of water on your head.

main_exercises.name: Decline Bench Reverse Crunch
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight; slow tempo, focusing on controlled lift rather than momentum
main_exercises.form_cue: Lift hips off the bench by curling the pelvis, not by swinging legs.

main_exercises.name: Front Plank with Shoulder Tap
main_exercises.load_guidance: Bodyweight; widen stance slightly if needed to maintain stability
main_exercises.form_cue: Keep hips level and minimize shifting as you tap each shoulder.

cooldown.description: Release core tension and restore spinal mobility.
movements: Child’s pose with deep breathing x 60s
Supine spinal twist x 45s per side

phase_notes.menstrual: Keep effort at the lower end of moderate and shorten sets if needed; focus on controlled reps and breathing rather than pushing fatigue. Swapping hanging work for floor-based options is a good adjustment.
phase_notes.follicular: You may feel more energized—lean into slightly stronger contractions and cleaner execution on rotational work like woodchoppers. This is a good phase to build consistency with form.
phase_notes.ovulatory: Core strength and coordination tend to feel sharp—challenge stability during carries and plank variations while maintaining excellent control. Avoid rushing reps despite higher energy.
phase_notes.early_luteal: Maintain steady effort and focus on time under tension, especially in slower movements like reverse crunches. Keep rest periods consistent to avoid unnecessary fatigue.
phase_notes.late_luteal: Reduce volume slightly if needed and prioritize stability over intensity, especially in dynamic movements like shoulder taps. Keep breathing slow and controlled to manage fatigue.
